headline: Upgrading Your Kitchen or Bathroom Plumbing: Mistakes to Avoid Before Remodeling
articleBody:
Reworking the plumbing in an older Salt Lake home sounds straightforward until walls come down. Small oversights during planning can derail your schedule, fail code inspections, or cause expensive water leaks down the road.

Common Mistakes to Avoid
- Closing walls before rough-in inspection: Concealed supply lines and drains must remain completely exposed until local inspectors sign off. Covering them early means tearing down fresh drywall.
- Forgetting shutoff access: Tucking water valves into unreachable corners makes future maintenance a nightmare. Always verify clear access points for every shutoff.
- Using estimated fixture dimensions: Buying faucets, freestanding tubs, or sink rough-ins without exact manufacturer spec sheets leads to rough plumbing that misses your cabinetry cutouts by inches.
- Overlooking proper venting: Drains require correct atmospheric venting to prevent gurgling and sewer gas intrusion. Altering drain paths without venting adjustments ruins performance.
- Skipping official permits: Assuming minor line shifts do not need city review can trigger stop-work orders and complicate future property sales.
